Fall is a big time for sports fans, and ESPN has just rolled out a major upgrade for its tvOS and iOS app users: 4K HDR streaming.

ESPN's streaming service now supports 4K HDR, with the tvOS and iOS apps the first to add support

Over the past few weeks, ESPN has begun rolling out a major upgrade across its tvOS and iOS apps.

The streaming service now offers 4K HDR picture quality for top-tier programming, including live events such as the NFL, NBA, and NHL.

Starting this week, ESPN and ESPN2 will begin broadcasting in 4K HDR in the United States, enhancing picture quality for fans during the most-watched sporting events of the year. This includes all of ESPN's Monday Night Football, NBA, and NHL games, as well as select college football and US Open tennis broadcasts, plus marquee live events such as Super Bowl LXI. The update will bring sharper edges, more vibrant colors, and smoother motion—elements that are essential to delivering a richer, more immersive viewing experience for sports fans. ESPN's iOS and tvOS apps will be the first to support the new experience, with other connected TV platforms to follow later. ESPN Unlimited subscribers on Disney+ in the United States will also have access to this feature.

When browsing the ESPN app, you'll notice a new "4K HDR" label added to content that supports higher-quality streaming.

As long as you have a stable internet connection, whether indoors or outdoors, 4K HDR will deliver more vivid, sharper, and higher-quality visuals for your favorite sports content.

For anyone planning to pick up an Apple TV 4K for the first time, we'd recommend holding off for a moment. Reports suggest a new-generation Apple TV model is almost ready to go.

Since ESPN launched its 4K HDR content, have you watched it? How was it? Let us know in the comments.
